title: Kruger National Park & the Panorama Route: a guide for nature lovers
excerpt: The Big Five in one of Africa's greatest reserves, and the canyon views of the Panorama Route next door — how to make the most of both.

body.p: Kruger is where many people see their first lion. Covering nearly two million hectares of bushveld in the north-east of South Africa, it is home to the Big Five — lion, leopard, elephant, rhino and buffalo — along with giraffe, zebra, cheetah, wild dog and hundreds of bird species.

body.h: Inside the park or a private reserve?

body.p: The national park itself has well-run rest camps and excellent roads. Along its western edge, the private reserves of the Greater Kruger share the same wildlife without fences, and add open-vehicle game drives with expert rangers, off-road tracking and night drives. For a first safari we usually recommend a private-reserve lodge.

ul: An early-morning game drive, when the predators are most active
Breakfast back at the lodge and a slow midday by the pool
An afternoon drive into the evening, with a sundowner in the bush
Dinner under the stars, with the sounds of the night all around

body.p: On the escarpment above Kruger, the Panorama Route is one of South Africa's most scenic drives. The Blyde River Canyon is one of the largest canyons on earth, and its green slopes are at their most dramatic from the Three Rondavels viewpoint. Along the way, God's Window looks out over the Lowveld, the river has carved extraordinary shapes at Bourke's Luck Potholes, and Lisbon Falls plunges into a deep gorge.
A full day is enough to see the highlights, and it makes a perfect break between game-drive days — our Kruger trips include it.

The dry winter months (roughly May to September) are best for game viewing: the bush thins out and animals gather at the water. Summer is green and lush, with newborn animals and superb birdlife, though some days are hot and wet. Kruger lies in a malaria area, so speak to a travel doctor before you go.
